name: inprocess-obi-apb-ibex-timer-compare-f5-fuzz
notes: The same CPU, DMA, windows, F1 program length and bounded wait as configs/scenarios/inprocess-obi-apb-ibex-timer-overflow-baseline-fuzz.json; the only difference is the declared IRQ source, which comes from configs/behaviors/pulp_timer_compare_f5.json: irq_o[1] (timer0_compare), 24 delivery ticks, trigger [[4,0],[8,3],[0,3]], status TIMER0_CMP offset 8

the scenario states no inline F5 facts: the entry merges the behavior file's facts into the declaration before f5_declaration, and the executor still cross-checks the bit, the three register offsets and the readable status word against configs/peripherals/pulp_timer_irq/component_profile.json

the declared trigger value 3 is the example vector the fuzzer seeds from and the corpus mutates; a case whose COUNT/CTRL words no longer equal the CMP word raises no IRQ and is reported as a timed-out case (wait_timeout 1, irq_edges 0), which is the expected exploration class
the timer declares 50 MHz, the CPU 50 MHz and the ZipDMA a nominal 1 Hz simulation rate, so assume_single_clock states that one host tick drives all three models

two IRQ sources share the one CPU input: the target's pulse on irq_o[1] and the ZipDMA completion level, in that declared order; a third source (the second timer0 bit or the timer1 bits) cannot be added to this build, see docs/reports/irq-declaration-expansion-20261101.md
